text: This book defines a tangent vector at p as a derivation of C^∞(M): a linear map v : C^∞(M) → ℝ satisfying which Leibniz-type rule?
explanation: A derivation at p is linear and obeys the product (Leibniz) rule v(fg) = f(p) v(g) + g(p) v(f), evaluating the undifferentiated factor at p. This coordinate-free definition yields the basis ∂/∂xⁱ|_p with components vⁱ = v(xⁱ). The multiplicative forms v(fg) = v(f) v(g) or v(f+g) = v(f) v(g) describe algebra homomorphisms, not derivations, and violate linearity.
